notes.text: Winter 2027: Course Offerings & Enrollment Information

The winter schedule of classes posts on Thursday, November 5th, and registration begins on Monday, November 9th. Please send any questions you have through the VAC and check out our Advising Calendar for up-to-date advising availability. Only drop-in advising is available in during registration so that the advisors are available to all public health students who have scheduling questions. If you are unable to come in during drop-in advising hours, please send any questions you have through the VAC. Queries received via phone or email will not receive a response.
We encourage students to read our Winter 2027 Enrollment Advice e-mail thoroughly.
Enrollment Updates
Our enrollment webpage will continue to be updated as new information becomes available.
WI27 PH 193 Enrollment:

Enrollment in the Public Health capstone sequence requires Department Approval for all students prior to enrollment. Students who have completed all PH 193 prerequisites or are completing their final PH 193 prerequisites in FA26 MUST submit their course preferences via Google form.
No students will be given clearance to enroll until after Fall grades have posted.
Students sending TEA requests or VAC messages about PH 193/194 enrollment will be redirected to this page.
WI27 PH 194 Enrollment:
This class is only for students who will have minimally completed PH 40, PH 101, PH 102, PH 110, PH 120, and PH 193 prior to WI27. Clearance to enroll will happen after PH 193 grades have posted.

Enrollment in the Public Health capstone sequence requires Department Approval for all students prior to enrollment. Students MUST complete the Google form to submit their time preferences in order to obtain authorization to enroll.
Students sending TEA requests or VAC messages about PH 193/194 enrollment will be redirected to this page.
WI27 PH 196AH Enrollment:

Enrollment in the Public Health Honors Practicum requires Department Approval for all students prior to enrollment. Students who have been accepted into the Honors Practicum will receive clearance to enroll after second pass has concluded during open registration for all students, or after grades have posted for students who are finishing their final prerequisites in FA26.
Courses Requiring TEA Authorization
The following courses require enrollment authorization through the TEA system:
Section 001: Doctor-Patient Interaction (Anne White)
Section 002: Health Promotion (Chris Zoumas)
Section 001: Health Access & Leadership (Ellen Beck)
PH 98/198 (Special Studies)
PH 99/199 (Special Studies)
Pedagogical Learning Assistant (PLA) Opportunities
Students interested in serving as a PLA should contact the course instructor directly to discuss available opportunities.
Please note:
You may not serve as a PLA or UGIA for a course in which you have previously held that role.
Students may serve as a PLA or UGIA no more than two total times, regardless of course or department.
No exceptions can be made to these policies.
For more information please see the PLA page.
Advising

You can check out our Advising Calendar for up-to-date advising availability. Only drop-in advising is available in during registration so that the advisors are available to all public health students who have scheduling questions. If you are unable to come in during zoom drop-in advising hours, please send any questions you have through the VAC. Queries received via phone or email will not receive a response.

As a reminder, it is very important that you check your VAC and UCSD email regularly. The program will be sending out time-sensitive updates. If you miss these updates, you may end up not getting seats in classes you need.
Note Regarding all PH Courses
If you are interested in enrolling in a PH course that is full during your first pass, you should waitlist at the very beginning of second pass.
In-Person versus Remote PH Instruction

A majority of our PH courses will be in-person for Winter 2027. Courses that offer an in-person option will indicate a campus classroom. All remote courses will list RCLAS indicating the course will be taught remotely.

PH 102R is offered fully remotely in the Winter, except for an in-person out-of-class midterm exam and an in-person out-of-class final, as listed. You must plan to attend the midterm and final as specified.
PH 158R is offered fully remotely in the Winter.

Prerequisites: PH 40, PH 101, PH 102, PH 110, PH 120, declared BSPH Major.

Enrollment in the Public Health capstone sequence requires Department Approval for all students prior to enrollment. Students who have completed all PH 193 prerequisites before Fall 2026 MUST submit their course preferences via Google form.
No students will be given clearance to enroll until after Fall grades have posted.
Students sending TEA requests or VAC messages about PH 193/194 enrollment will be redirected to this page.

Note: As a reminder all Capstone students are required to attend their PH 194 final exam Poster Session in-person, there are no exceptions. Please see below for attendance policy for the course and Poster Showcase.
Remnder: PH 193 is offered in the Fall and Winter quarters.
BSPH Program Policy on Maximum Number of Absences

The BSPH Program policy includes that students must attend a minimum of 80% of each Capstone course in the sequence or the Honors Practicum sequence. Students will not pass PH 193/194 or PH 196AH/BH if they miss >20% of classes (for any reason). Regardless of a student's earned grade, any student who has missed more than the allowed number of absences (excused or unexcused) will fail the course and need to retake the course in a future quarter.
PH 194/PH 196BH Final: Poster Showcase Presentation

The final for PH 194 and PH 196BH is an in-person poster presentation of the Capstone project or Honors Practicum project at the Poster Showcase. The Poster Showcase is the final step in students culminating research project. It is designed to give students an in-person experience of sharing and discussing work with peers and faculty the same way that is expected of many public health professionals. It is an essential step in preparation for a career in the field of public health and a required final event of this PH 194 Capstone course and the PH 196BH course. Attendance to this event is mandatory for all students to pass the course. Students failing to attend will be required to retake the course in a future quarter. The final requirement of participating in the Poster Showcase is not merely a formality but a pivotal component of the students’ comprehensive research experience. It is crafted to provide a realistic experience that mirrors the professional expectations placed upon public health professionals. Engaging in this forum allows students to convey and deliberate over their findings with both peers and faculty, fostering a collaborative and scholarly environment. This Poster Showcase is indispensable in the academic and professional journey within the public health sphere. It equips students with the vital skills of communication, critical feedback reception, and networking, which are cornerstone abilities in the field. Moreover, it prepares them for the real-world scenario where sharing and defending their research findings is a common practice among public health professionals. The presentation and subsequent question-and-answer session are designed to simulate the professional conferences and symposiums where experts convene to exchange ideas and advance public health knowledge.
